class.name: GrassField3D
class.brief_description: Procedural grass blades around the camera, with wind, clumps and LOD.
class.description: Grows real blade geometry in square tiles around the current camera, out to [member radius]. Blades sit on a jittered world grid seeded by position, so the same ground always grows the same blades; neighbouring blades are grouped into clumps that share height, facing, lean and dryness. Where a [TerrainDataMap3D] is set in [member data_map], blades stand on its height and [member rules] (a [PlantSpecies]) decides where they grow (slope, wetness, water depth, distance to water); without one they grow flat at this node's height. Each blade is a quadratic Bezier strip bent in the vertex shader by the wind from [WeatherMap3D] when one is present, else by [member fallback_wind], with its length preserved. Far tiles keep fewer blades (by a fixed rank per blade, so thinning never reshuffles) and widen them to keep the coverage. Rain from the weather map darkens and smooths the blades, and bodies in [member trample_group] lay them down (see [member trample_enabled]). Tiles are ordinary MultiMeshes, so the path tracer sees every blade.

method.name: get_hay_bale_count
method.description: The round bales lying in this node's hay meadows now (baled on the fourth day, carted on the fifth).

method.name: get_mown_days_at
method.description: Days since the hay meadow of [member hay_meadows] over [param position] was mown, or -1 outside them or before their mowing day.

method.name: mown_days_at
method.description: [method get_mown_days_at] over every GrassField3D in the tree with hay meadows (the largest), -1 where none is mown. [VegetationField3D] reads it to cut its tall herbs (PlantGenerator species over 12 cm) with the sward until they grow back, 28 days on.

method.name: advance_lodging
method.description: Steps the whole lodging grid (see [member lodging]) by [param weather_seconds] at once, reading the weather as it is now: for time skips and tests.

method.name: crop_calendar_stage
method.description: The BBCH growth stage on [param day] (of the year) of a cereal sown on [param sown_day], from a temperate sowing calendar (winter crops sown from day 200; spring crops otherwise). Harvested (99) from [param harvest_day], or about ten days after hard dough when it is negative, until the next sowing.

method.name: crop_canopy_look
method.description: The crop seen from a distance at [param stage]: its colour (sRGB) and, in alpha, how much of the soil it covers.

method.name: get_burn_cover_at
method.description: The sward's cover on burnt ground at [param global_position]: 0 on a fresh burn, 1 where the ground never burnt or has recovered (see [member burn_recovery]).

method.name: get_lodging_at
method.description: Storm lodging at [param global_position]: x is the share of blades lying down (0..1), y and z the world direction they lie in. Zero outside the grid round the camera.

method.name: get_fairy_ring_at
method.description: The meadow fairy ring bands at [param global_position] (see [member fairy_rings]), 0 to 1 each: x the dark front, y the dead band, z the inner dark band. One world layout: [constant PlantSpecies.RULE_FAIRY_RING] places the ring's mushrooms on the same rings.

method.name: get_far_color
method.description: The field seen from a distance, linear: the colour the ground under the grass takes where the blades have thinned away ([code]grass_ground_far[/code]), and the grass layer of [member VegetationField3D.cover_grass]. Measured from a small render of the field's own blades a few frames after it enters the tree and after each change to its look ([signal far_color_changed]); a hand-matched blend of its colours before that and without a RenderingDevice.

method.name: get_far_color_lobes
method.description: How the far colour changes with the sun's azimuth from the view, [code]phi[/code]: two colours [code]l1[/code], [code]l2[/code], per channel, for the factor [code]1 + l1 cos(phi) + l2 cos(2 phi)[/code] the ground under far grass takes ([code]phi[/code] 0: the sun behind the viewer, where a sward is brightest). Fitted to the render of the blades with the sun at four headings; zero before that.

method.name: get_far_published
method.description: What this field publishes for the far ground at the current sun: [code]far[/code] (the far colour at the sun's elevation), [code]lobe1[/code] and [code]lobe2[/code] (its azimuth lobes there), [code]scale[/code] (that colour over the far cover map's, the global [code]grass_ground_far_scale[/code]), [code]sun[/code] (heading x, z and azimuth strength, the global [code]grass_ground_sun[/code]), [code]sun_elevation[/code] in degrees, [code]cover_share[/code] and [code]baked[/code], and the live-view match ([member far_match_view]): [code]view_scale[/code] (the factor on both colours), [code]view_ratio[/code] (blades over far ground on screen at the last look), [code]view_pairs[/code], [code]view_round[/code], [code]view_state[/code] (0 idle, 1 waiting, 2 reading) and [code]view_msec[/code] (the last look's sampling time). For checking a scene's far blend, since global shader parameters cannot be read back at runtime.

method.name: get_effective_dryness
method.description: The dryness the blades and ground show: [member dryness] browned by the season (see [member season_source]).

method.name: get_ring_blade_count
method.description: Returns the number of blades in the far rings' tiles (see [member far_rings]).

method.name: get_ring_build_msec
method.description: Returns the time, in milliseconds, the last frame that built far ring tiles spent on them.

method.name: get_ring_tile_count
method.description: Returns the number of far ring tiles.

method.name: get_season_green
method.description: The sward's greenness from the last season read, 0 to 1 (1 without a [member season_source]).

method.name: get_flood_wash_at
method.description: The sward under the last flood's mark at [param position] (see [member flood_wash]): x combed flat (0 to 1), y silted (0 to 1), z the days since the peak; z -1 above the mark or with no flood known ([method WorldWater.high_water_at]).

method.name: get_snowmelt_at
method.description: The sward after the snow at [param position] (see [member snowmelt]), on day of year [param day] (below 1: the season's day): x the days the last lasting snowpack lay, y the days since it melted (-1 while snow lies or without a lasting pack), z the matting, 0 to 1. Without a weather climate (no [WeatherMap3D]): all zero.

method.name: get_shell_column_count
method.description: Returns the number of voxel columns in the far shell (see [member far_shell]).

method.name: get_shell_tile_count
method.description: Returns the number of far shell tiles.

method.name: is_far_color_baked
method.description: [code]true[/code] once [method get_far_color] comes from the render of the blades.

method.name: add_trample
method.description: Presses the grass at [param position] within [param radius] metres, as a mover does: flat under it, bent away from it at its rim and forward along [param velocity]. [param strength] scales the bend (0 to 1). Use it for footsteps, landings or anything not in [member trample_group].

method.name: clear_trample
method.description: Stands every trampled blade back up at once.

method.name: get_blade_count
method.description: Returns the number of blades in all live tiles. With [member gpu_fill] it counts the candidates sent to the shader, including those the rules then leave empty.

method.name: get_build_time_msec
method.description: Returns the time, in milliseconds, of the last frame that built tiles.

method.name: get_ground_shader_code
method.description: Returns shader code for a terrain material: [code]grass_ground(world_pos, albedo)[/code] mixes [param albedo] towards [member ground_tint] where this field's rules let grass grow, and [code]grass_ground_cover(world_pos)[/code] returns that coverage (0 to 1). Paste it into the terrain's shader; it reads the [code]grass_ground_*[/code] global uniforms this node publishes. Also [code]grass_ground_specular(world_pos, specular)[/code]: the ground's specular under the sward (the blades hide the soil's sheen), for the ground shader's [code]SPECULAR[/code].

method.name: get_material
method.description: Returns the blade [ShaderMaterial], built on first use. Its shader parameters can be read but are set from this node's properties.

method.name: update_flood_map
method.description: Reads the last flood's mark round [param center] again now (see [member flood_wash]); the field does so on its own every 5 s.

method.name: get_tile_count
method.description: Returns the number of live tiles.

method.name: get_trample_at
method.description: Returns the trample bend at [param position]: a world x/z direction whose length is the amount, from 0 (upright) to 1 (flat). Zero outside the trample field.

method.name: is_gpu_fill_available
method.description: Whether [member gpu_fill] can run: there is a [RenderingDevice] and the fill's compute shader built.

method.name: is_still_frozen
method.description: With [member still_shot]: [code]true[/code] once it has settled and stopped updating.

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Frees every tile; they are built again around the camera on the next frames.

method.name: season_greenness
method.description: How green a temperate sward is for a season state ([method WeatherMap3D.get_season]), 0 to 1: grassland greenness follows soil water and temperature (PhenoGrass, Hufkens et al. 2016; the Growing Season Index of Jolly et al. 2005 without its day-length term, as a temperate sward stays green through short days). [code]smoothstep(0.1, 0.4, soil_moisture) * smoothstep(-8, 2, temperature)[/code]: a summer drought browns it, a hard winter leaves it tan, a mild wet winter keeps it green. 1 for an empty state.

method.name: get_field_stage
method.description: The growth stage of [member fields] entry [param index] now.

method.name: update_at
method.description: Builds and frees tiles around [param center] now, as the node does each frame around the camera. Useful without a camera or in tests.

members.member: Blade colour at the root.

Years the sward takes to grow back over burnt ground ([code]WorldFire.burn_age_at[/code]): gone on a fresh burn, short sparse blades first, full cover after this many years. The rules' [member PlantSpecies.burn_recovery] wins when it is set. 0 leaves the grass blind to fire. The ages are read once a bake, so a live fire shows after the next [method rebuild].
Minimum and maximum blade height, in metres. Each clump picks a height in this range.
Segments along each blade. 4 bends smoothly; 1 (a single triangle) suits a short, dense undercoat at a quarter of the vertices.
Blade width at the root, in metres.

Path to a [VegetationField3D] whose canopy species shade the ground (see [method VegetationField3D.get_shade_at]). When [member rules] narrows [member PlantSpecies.shade_range], blades and the ground tint follow that shade: for example [code]Vector2(0, 0.4)[/code] keeps a meadow sward out from under the trees. Call [method rebuild] after the field is populated again.
Size of a clump, in metres. Blades in a clump share height, facing, lean and dryness.
How much blade colour varies: large patches and single blades drift towards yellower or bluer greens and lighter or darker values. 0 gives every blade the same colours.

A cereal grown instead of grass: each record is a tiller (a stem, four leaves and the ear, with awns for barley and rye, or the open panicle of oats) as real geometry, set in drill rows [member row_spacing] apart along [member drill_angle], one to three tillers to a plant. [member density] is then tillers per square metre (400 to 600 in a wheat crop) and [member crop_stage] sets the look. Built on the CPU for now ([member gpu_fill] is ignored). Keep [member tile_size] small enough that a tile stays under the path tracer's merged BLAS triangle cap: 1.5 m at 400 tillers per square metre.

The crop's growth stage on the BBCH (Zadoks) decimal scale: below 10 nothing has emerged; 10 to 29 leaves and tillers only; 30 to 49 the stem elongates; 51 to 59 the ear emerges; 71 to 89 the grain fills and ripens, the ear and then the straw turning from green to gold while the leaves die from the bottom up and the ears nod (barley hangs right over, wheat stays upright); 99 harvested, leaving stubble about 15 cm high. Changing it only sets shader parameters, except across 10.
Path to a [TerrainDataMap3D] giving the ground height and the maps [member rules] read.
Blades per square metre near the camera.
The direction the crop's rows run, in radians from +X towards +Z. Rows of one 3 m drill bout wander together, so the bouts show across a field.
Tip colour of dry blades.
Fraction of blades with dry tips. A third of those are dead from the root (thatch).

If [code]true[/code], the widest field checks its far colour against the frame: once the far colour is baked, and again when the sun's elevation moves more than 8 degrees or the camera travels more than [member radius], it reads the frame back asynchronously and compares pairs of ground points in the same direction from the camera, one where the blades stand full and one just past the fade band, then scales the published far colour's brightness (and [code]grass_ground_far_scale[/code]) until they agree within 3% (at most five rounds, factor 0.5 to 1.5; pixels that read as sky, haze or water are left out). This takes up lighting the bake's plain ground plane does not reproduce, so the field ends without a lighter or darker ring.
Wind velocity (x, z) in metres per second, used when no [WeatherMap3D] publishes wind.
Distance from the camera, in metres, to which the far rings reach. They thin out over the last fifth of it as the far shell rises.

Past the near tiles, one set of wider blades with fewer vertices out to [member far_ring_range], thinned with the square of the distance by each blade's own rank and widened to keep the sward's cover (Ghost of Tsushima, Wohllaib GDC 2021). They fade in over the near tiles' outer band, so no ring or seam shows. Only the widest meadow field (not a crop) grows them.

Past the far rings, the sward as voxel columns standing on the ground out to [member far_shell_range]: real geometry in the far ground's own colour, so raster and the path tracer see the same shape. It rises out of the ground as the rings thin out and sinks back at its end.
Distance from the camera, in metres, where the far shell has sunk back into the ground.

The blades' specular as fibres: ANISOTROPY spreading the highlight across each blade (its normals vary across its width, not along it), so a sward reads as a mass of fine fibres with a sheen running over it, as hair does. Raster and the path tracer shade it alike. Wet, frosted, muddy or snowy blades lose it. 0 turns it off.

Hay meadows mown in the sward, each a Dictionary: [code]polygon[/code] ([PackedVector2Array], world xz), [code]row_angle[/code] (radians, the mower's passes and the rows along world [code](cos, sin)[/code] in xz), and either [code]mow_day[/code] (the day of the year it is mown, read from [member season_source]) or [code]days[/code] (fixed days since mown). The sward is cut to a 7.5 to 10 cm stubble that grows back over about six weeks; the cut grass lies in the mower's swaths on the day, is tedded flat over the next two, raked into windrows on the third, baled on the fourth (round bales of [method PlantGenerator.make_hay_bale] dropped along the rows, a bale's hay apart, from the first layer that holds the meadow) and carted from the fifth, curing from green to a green-gold hay. [VegetationField3D] herbs over 12 cm stand as their stalks cut at the stubble for 28 days. All in the shader: the days pass without a rebuild. Set the same meadows on every layer of a sward (undercoat, turf).

With a [member crop]: the fields it grows in, each a [Dictionary]. [code]polygon[/code] ([PackedVector2Array], world XZ) is required; optional [code]drill_angle[/code] and [code]row_spacing[/code] (default the node's), [code]stage[/code] (a fixed BBCH stage; default the node's [member crop_stage]), [code]sown_day[/code] and [code]harvest_day[/code] (days of the year: with a [member season_source] the stage follows a sowing calendar, autumn sowing from day 200 over-wintering, spring sowing through in five months, stubble from harvest to the next sowing), [code]tramline_spacing[/code] (default 24 m; 0 none: paired unsown wheel tracks [code]tramline_gauge[/code] apart, default 1.8 m) and [code]headland[/code] (default 12 m; 0 none: rows run round the edge where the drill turned). Outside the fields nothing grows. Up to 63 fields a node. The ground shader ([method get_ground_shader_code]) draws the drilled soil and darker wheelings under every crop node's fields and, past the tillers, the crop's own colour and cover at its stage ([method crop_canopy_look]). Harvested fields (99) carry the combine's straw swaths, one down each pass (a third of [code]tramline_spacing[/code], or 7.5 m), as lying straw near and paler stripes far off. Grass fields without a crop and [VegetationField3D] plants keep out of every crop node's fields.

Fill each tile's blades with a compute shader instead of the CPU loop. The CPU lists the cells the tile keeps at its level and bakes [member rules] into a 0.5 m grid; the shader makes every blade from the same hashes, clumps and light and writes the records straight into the tile's [MultiMesh] ([method RenderingServer.multimesh_mark_buffer_rd_changed]), so the path tracer sees them as before. The blades match the CPU path except within a few centimetres of a rule's edge; the main-thread cost of a tile drops by about 40%. Falls back to the CPU without a [RenderingDevice].

Height (m) the sward is grazed to where deer browse hard ([method WorldStand.browse_at]): a dense, even lawn with torn pale blade ends, eased in from pressure 0.3 to 0.8. Done in the shader from a pressure grid over the map, followed when the stand changes, so it needs no rebuild. 0 leaves the sward ungrazed.
Colour the ground takes under the grass (the shaded thatch between blades), with alpha as the strength. Read by terrain shaders through [method get_ground_shader_code].

If [code]true[/code], this field publishes its coverage and [member ground_tint] as the [code]grass_ground_*[/code] global uniforms. With several fields, enable it on the one that covers the most ground.

Meadow fairy rings in the blades: rings 4 to 28 m across (in three of ten 40 m cells, some broken into arcs) with a band of dark, lush, taller grass at the front, a browned, thinned dead band behind it and a weaker dark band inside (Shantz and Piemeisel 1917). Computed in the shader from world position, so it costs no memory or rebuild. Never in crops.

Storm lodging: where gusts on wet, tall sward pass the stems' base strength (critical 2 m gust 10 m/s for a 0.6 m sward, lower when wet or raining, varying in patches), the blades go down in swirled patches along the wind and stand again over a few days (crops: weeks). Read from [WorldWeather] on a 384 m grid of 4 m cells round the camera, eight rows a frame, and handed to the shader as a texture, so it needs no rebuild.
Largest lean of a blade at rest, in metres of tip offset per metre of height.

Rocks on the ground that no blade grows through: each a disc (x, ground y, z, radius), the radius where the rock meets the soil, as [member VegetationField3D.obstacles]. Blades root 2 cm or more off a rock, on both fill paths. Setting it rebuilds the field. Mounds the [member undergrowth_field] or [member canopy_field] places (species with the meta [code]sward_mound[/code], [method PlantGenerator.make_mounds]) are kept out the same way, followed as they come and go.
Distance from the camera, in metres, to which tiles are grown. 0 draws no blades at all (no near tiles, far rings or shell), for a field kept only for its rules or ground tint.
The distance between the crop's drill rows, in metres (12 to 15 cm for cereals).

Where grass grows: the rules of a [PlantSpecies] over the maps of [member data_map]. Its spacing, footprint and meshes are ignored. Without rules, grass grows on dry land only. With a narrowed [member PlantSpecies.spring_range] it is an oasis sward: it grows only round the desert springs ([constant PlantSpecies.RULE_SPRING]), on the sand seas' damp corridors. Any sward on a sand sea also comes back onto the sand where an oasis's ground is wet.
How much the season browns the sward, 0 (not at all) to 1.

Path to a [WeatherMap3D] whose season ([method WeatherMap3D.get_season]) turns the sward through the year: once a second its greenness ([method season_greenness]) raises the blades' and the ground's dryness towards all thatch (effective dryness [code]dryness + (1 - dryness) (1 - green) season_response[/code]), and the far colour is measured again when that moves by more than 0.05. Empty: [member dryness] as set.

The sward after a long snow lie: where the season's snowpack (the weather's degree-day pack, by height) lay more than about 20 days, blades lie matted flat in swirls and pale for about three weeks after the melt; past about 45 days, grey snow mould patches (Typhula, a few cm to 30 cm) show as grey lint that dries to straw and greens over in a few weeks. Snow-drift noise moves the lie by metres. Off for crops.

The sward under the last flood's mark ([method WorldWater.high_water_at]): blades combed flat along the flow at the peak and grey with silt, with a sharp line at the crest, standing again over about five weeks while the silt pales over about four months. Read on a 64-cell grid of 6 m round the camera every 5 s ([method update_flood_map] now). Off for crops.

For still shots on a tight memory budget (benches on the cloud): once the near tiles, far rings and shell round the camera are complete, the field stops updating (no rebuilds, no trample) until the camera moves 0.5 m or the field is rebuilt. [method is_still_frozen] says when it has settled.

Path to the [DirectionalLight3D] whose heading turns the far grass colour (see [method get_far_color_lobes]). Empty: the first visible [DirectionalLight3D] in the field's world. The widest field publishes it with the camera position as [code]grass_ground_sun[/code] and [code]grass_ground_view[/code]; the effect lessens as the sun climbs and is off with the sun down.
Edge of a tile, in metres.
Blade colour at the tip.
If [code]true[/code], movers lay the grass down and it springs back. The field covers [member trample_size] around the camera.

Every [Node3D] in this group tramples the grass while its underside is within the blades. Its radius comes from the meta [code]trample_radius[/code], else its first [CollisionShape3D] (sphere, capsule, cylinder or box), else [member trample_radius].
Radius, in metres, of a mover with neither a [code]trample_radius[/code] meta nor a collision shape.
Half-life, in seconds, of the bend: trampled blades stand halfway back up in this time. 0 springs back at once.
Texels a side of the trample field. Higher keeps narrower trails.
Edge, in metres, of the square trample field around the camera.

Path to a [VegetationField3D] whose tall undergrowth (species with [member PlantSpecies.sward_shade]) shades the sward out: blades thin by [method VegetationField3D.get_sward_shade_at] under its bracken and bramble stands. Usually the herb field, which may differ from [member canopy_field].
How much a blade seen edge-on widens across the view (Ghost of Tsushima's view-space thickening), so the field looks full from every side. 0 turns it off.
How far blades bend for a given wind speed.

Worn paths, the same format as [member VegetationField3D.paths]. Along a path the sward thins and shortens by [member trample_resistance], and the ground tint shows the bare trodden soil. Changing it rebuilds the tiles. The world's game trails ([code]WorldStand.get_trails()[/code], published from [method VegetationField3D.make_game_trails]) are worn the same way, on top of these, and followed when they change.
Walkers a year on a path that halve the sward's cover. Grasses resist trampling well (Cole 1995); 0 turns paths off for this field.

signal.name: far_color_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the render of the blades has given a new [method get_far_color].

constants.constant: Bread wheat: an awnless, flattened ear held upright, about 0.8 m of straw.
Two-row barley: a slim ear with long awns that bends right over when ripe.
Oats: an open panicle of drooping spikelets on whorled branches.
Rye: the tallest, about 1.25 m, a long slender ear with short awns and blue-grey leaves.
